paragraphs.text_en: ThinkRec: Thinking-based Recommendation via LLM
paragraphs.text_zh: ThinkRec：基于思考的 LLM 推荐方法

paragraphs.text_en: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have enabled more semantic-aware recommendations through natural language generation. Existing LLM for recommendation (LLM4Rec) methods mostly operate in a System 1-like manner, relying on superficial features to match similar items based on click history, rather than reasoning through deeper behavioral logic. This often leads to superficial and erroneous recommendations. Inspired by this, we propose ThinkRec, a thinking-based framework that shifts LLM4Rec from an intuitive system to a rational system. First, ThinkRec introduces a thinking activation mechanism by injecting synthetic reasoning traces, making the recommendation process resemble the Chain of Thought (CoT) reasoning of LLMs. This mechanism analyzes interaction histories, identifies user preferences, and makes decisions based on target items. Furthermore, considering the highly diverse distribution of recommendation data, we propose an instance-wise expert fusion mechanism to reduce the reasoning difficulty. By dynamically assigning weights to expert models based on users’ latent features, ThinkRec adapts its reasoning path to individual users, thereby enhancing precision and personalization. Extensive experiments on various real-world web user behavior preference datasets demonstrate that ThinkRec significantly outperforms baselines in terms of recommendation accuracy and interpretability, providing superior recommendations based on a deeper understanding of user intent and a more rigorous reasoning process. Code is available in https://github.com/Yu-Qi-hang/ThinkRec.
paragraphs.text_zh: 近年来大语言模型（LLM）的进展使得基于自然语言生成的、更具语义感知能力的推荐成为可能。现有的 LLM4Rec 方法大多以类似 System 1 的方式运作，仅依赖表层特征根据点击历史匹配相似物品，而没有通过更深层的行为逻辑进行推理，这往往导致表层化甚至错误的推荐结果。受此启发，我们提出 ThinkRec —— 一个基于思考的框架，将 LLM4Rec 从直觉式系统推向理性系统。首先，ThinkRec 通过注入合成推理轨迹引入了一种思考激活机制，使推荐过程类似于 LLM 的 Chain-of-Thought (CoT) 推理：分析交互历史、识别用户偏好、并基于目标物品做出决策。其次，考虑到推荐数据分布高度多样，我们提出了一种实例级专家融合机制以降低推理难度——根据用户潜在特征动态地为各专家模型分配权重，使 ThinkRec 能够针对个体用户调整推理路径，从而提升精度与个性化能力。在多个真实世界 web 用户行为偏好数据集上的大量实验表明，ThinkRec 在推荐准确率与可解释性上都显著优于 baseline，能够基于对用户意图的更深理解和更严谨的推理过程提供更优的推荐。代码见 https://github.com/Yu-Qi-hang/ThinkRec。

paragraphs.text_en: 1 Introduction
paragraphs.text_zh: 1 引言

paragraphs.text_en: Recommendation systems are indispensable in modern digital platforms, enabling users to navigate vast content efficiently [9, 13, 29]. Traditional sequential recommendation methods rely on implicit modeling of user interaction histories and are limited in their ability to model context and incorporate broader knowledge, which restricts their reasoning and generalization capabilities. Recent advances in LLMs offer strong contextual comprehension and extensive world knowledge to improve recommendation systems.
paragraphs.text_zh: 推荐系统在现代数字平台中不可或缺，能够帮助用户在海量内容中高效导航 [9, 13, 29]。传统的序列推荐方法依赖于对用户交互历史的隐式建模，在建模上下文与引入更广泛知识方面能力有限，制约了它们的推理与泛化能力。LLM 的最新进展为推荐系统提供了强大的上下文理解能力和广阔的世界知识。

paragraphs.text_en: Prior LLM4Rec paradigms can be separated into three categories: (1) item scoring [23, 46], where LLMs answer binary preference questions given user and item context; (2) item generation [2, 3, 6, 20], which maps natural language prompts to item IDs through aligned embedding spaces or semantic identifiers; and (3) hybrid modeling [8, 44], where a single LLM performs multiple tasks such as point-wise prediction, pair-wise ranking, or list-wise generation. Although these LLM4Rec methods differ in output formats and representation learning strategies, they fundamentally resemble System 1—the intuitive system—in cognitive science [17]. They tend to match similar items based on click history, while overlooking the deeper behavioral logic. This limitation becomes evident in cases such as the one shown in Figure 1(b), where the user’s behavior
paragraphs.text_zh: 已有的 LLM4Rec 范式可以分为三类：(1) 物品打分 [23, 46]，由 LLM 在给定用户与物品上下文的情况下回答二元偏好问题；(2) 物品生成 [2, 3, 6, 20]，通过对齐的 embedding 空间或语义标识符将自然语言 prompt 映射为物品 ID；(3) 混合建模 [8, 44]，由单个 LLM 同时执行 point-wise 预测、pair-wise 排序、list-wise 生成等多种任务。尽管这些 LLM4Rec 方法在输出格式与表征学习策略上各有不同，但它们本质上都类似认知科学中的 System 1（直觉系统）[17]：根据点击历史匹配相似物品，而忽视了更深层的行为逻辑。这一局限在图 1(b) 等情形中尤为明显，例如其中用户的行为

paragraphs.text_en: over time is: dislikes “Dune”, likes “The Three-Body Problem”, and likes “Foundation” (all three are science fiction). Methods that rely on System 1-like intuition tend to infer that the user would also like “Hyperion” (science fiction) simply because it belongs to the same genre. In reality, the user might dislike philosophical or metaphysical themes in fiction, which are prominent in *Hyperion*, making it an unsuitable recommendation. Clearly, if we can leverage the vast knowledge in LLMs and fully activate their reasoning capabilities , recommendation performance can be significantly improved.
paragraphs.text_zh: 随时间变化为：不喜欢《沙丘》、喜欢《三体》、喜欢《基地》（三者皆为科幻作品）。依赖 System 1 式直觉的方法往往会推断该用户也会喜欢《海伯利安》（同为科幻），仅仅因为它属于同一题材。但实际上，该用户可能并不喜欢小说中浓厚的哲学或形而上主题，而这恰恰是《海伯利安》的核心，因此并非合适的推荐。显然，如果我们能够利用 LLM 的庞大知识储备并充分激活其推理能力，推荐性能将获得显著提升。

paragraphs.text_en: This motivates our effort to push LLM4Rec from a System 1 paradigm toward a more rational, System 2-like reasoning framework. Recent concurrent works have also explored latent reasoning [33, 47] or dual-head reasoning architectures [41] to address this. We raise two key questions for the advancement: 1) How to effectively balance recommendation objectives with language modeling tasks to fully exploit the reasoning capabilities of LLMs. Existing methods often prioritize direct recommendation metrics such as hit rate or ranking accuracy, overlooking LLMs’ strengths in semantic reasoning. However, blind reinforcement thinking can lead to simple next token prediction, defeating the goal of recommendation. 2) How to think more effectively in the presence of diverse user behaviors and underlying preferences. As shown in Figure 1(c), user behaviors vary widely, and uniform modeling tends to obscure personality preferences while distracting the model from salient signals, impairing its reasoning capacity. Moreover, inferring user intent solely from high-rating items and generic world knowledge limits the informational basis for accurate preference reasoning.
paragraphs.text_zh: 这促使我们将 LLM4Rec 从 System 1 范式推向更理性的、类似 System 2 的推理框架。近期的并行工作也尝试通过潜在推理 [33, 47] 或双头推理架构 [41] 来解决这一问题。我们提出推动这一方向的两个关键问题：1) 如何在推荐目标与语言建模任务之间取得有效平衡，从而充分释放 LLM 的推理能力？现有方法往往优先优化命中率或排序准确率等直接的推荐指标，忽视了 LLM 在语义推理方面的优势；然而盲目地强化思考又可能退化为简单的 next token prediction，背离了推荐的目标。2) 在用户行为多样、潜在偏好各异的情况下，如何更有效地进行思考？如图 1(c) 所示，用户行为差异巨大，统一建模容易掩盖个性化偏好，分散模型对显著信号的注意力，从而损害其推理能力；此外，仅根据高分物品和通用世界知识来推断用户意图，也限制了准确进行偏好推理的信息基础。

paragraphs.text_en: To address these challenges, we propose Thinking-based Recommendation via LLM, abbreviated as ThinkRec. One of the main problems faced is that the data and optimization goals of recommendation tasks lack the ability to activate thinking in LLMs (Challenge 1). To overcome this challenge, we designed the item augmentation
paragraphs.text_zh: 为应对上述挑战，我们提出 Thinking-based Recommendation via LLM，简称 ThinkRec。我们面临的核心问题之一是：推荐任务的数据与优化目标本身缺乏激活 LLM 思考能力的机制（挑战 1）。为克服这一挑战，我们设计了物品增强

paragraphs.text_en: and thinking activation framework for finetuning. The fine-tuned model analyzes associations in historical item information, determines user preferences, and gives explicit reasons while deriving recommendations. We extracted the metadata keywords of the items with the help of an existing summarization model as the augmentation information of the items to support the reasoning. In addition, reasoning data is synthesized using a strong reasoning model, and the reasoning capability is distilled to the local model by mixed sampling of reasoning and recommendation data. Therefore, item augmentation and thinking activation become a bridge connecting the recommendation task and the language task, making recommendations traceable. To address the difficulty of thinking diversely with rich information (Challenge 2), we add the user’s preferences (yes/no) of items to the prompts and generate personalized recommendation experts based on latent user features. In the technique, we design a dynamic Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) fusion method. Users are grouped by latent user features extracted with traditional recommendation models as shown in Figure 1(c). A set of base LoRAs can be fine-tuned using the grouped data and represented with corresponding user features. For each user, the engagement level of each LoRA can be determined through a gating mechanism. The difficulty of thinking is reduced through information classification and personalization mechanisms. In deployment, the reasoning ability internalized in model parameters allows ThinkRec to operate efficiently in the ranking stage: by constraining the output to a single token, the model produces batch-level results with just one forward pass.
paragraphs.text_zh: 与思考激活的 fine-tuning 框架。微调后的模型能够分析历史物品信息中的关联、判断用户偏好，并在给出推荐的同时显式说明理由。我们借助现有的摘要模型抽取物品的元数据关键词作为物品的增强信息，以支持推理。此外，使用一个强推理模型合成推理数据，并通过对推理数据与推荐数据的混合采样将推理能力蒸馏至本地模型。由此，物品增强与思考激活成为连接推荐任务与语言任务的桥梁，使推荐过程具备可追溯性。针对在丰富信息条件下进行多样化思考的难题（挑战 2），我们将用户对物品的偏好（yes/no）加入 prompt，并基于潜在用户特征生成个性化的推荐专家。在技术上，我们设计了一种动态 LoRA 融合方法：通过传统推荐模型抽取的潜在用户特征对用户分组（如图 1(c) 所示），用分组数据 fine-tune 一组 base LoRA 并以对应的用户特征作为其表征。对每个用户，通过门控机制确定每个 LoRA 的参与程度。借助信息分类与个性化机制，思考的难度被有效降低。在部署阶段，模型参数中已内化的推理能力使 ThinkRec 能在 ranking 阶段高效运行：通过将输出限制为单个 token，模型仅需一次前向传递即可产出 batch 级别的结果。

paragraphs.text_en: 2.1 LLM-based Recommendation
paragraphs.text_zh: 2.1 基于 LLM 的推荐

paragraphs.text_en: LLM-based Recommendation. With the rapid progress of LLMs, there has been growing interest in adapting them to recommendation tasks using both textual and structured data. Early works [4, 12, 21, 46] rely on prompt-based scoring by converting recommendations into binary question-answering, while others [14, 20, 22, 50] align language space with item embeddings to directly generate item IDs. More advanced approaches, such as P5 [7] and InstructRec [44] unify multiple sub-tasks—like rating prediction, pairwise comparison, or ranking, into a single language modeling framework. These methods demonstrate LLMs’ flexibility in expressing recommendation semantics, yet most focus on adapting output formats, treating LLMs as static scorers or selectors with limited interpretability. Beyond static prompting, recent efforts shift toward viewing LLMs as interactive agents capable of multi-step reasoning and personalized decision-making. For example, RecMind [34] and MACRec [35] introduce modularized reasoning structures, enabling planning-based recommendation. Others explore integrating LLMs into various stages of the pipeline—for instance, generating user or item representations [48] or acting as high-level decision controllers [30]. Meanwhile, instruction tuning [44], chain-of-thought prompting [24] have been proposed to enhance LLMs’ semantic understanding. Despite these developments, explicit reasoning supervision and fine-grained user modeling remain underexplored. ThinkRec addresses these gaps by integrating reasoning-augmented training and personalized expert fusion, enabling user-specific recommendations grounded in structured reasoning.
paragraphs.text_zh: 基于 LLM 的推荐。随着 LLM 的快速发展，将其同时利用文本与结构化数据来适配推荐任务的研究日益活跃。早期工作 [4, 12, 21, 46] 通过将推荐转化为二元问答，借助基于 prompt 的打分实现推荐；另一些工作 [14, 20, 22, 50] 则将语言空间与物品 embedding 对齐，从而直接生成物品 ID。更进一步，P5 [7] 与 InstructRec [44] 等方法将评分预测、pairwise 比较、ranking 等多个子任务统一进同一个语言建模框架。这些方法展示了 LLM 在表达推荐语义方面的灵活性，但大多聚焦于输出格式的适配，将 LLM 视为静态打分器或选择器，可解释性有限。在静态 prompting 之外，近期研究开始把 LLM 视为可进行多步推理与个性化决策的交互式 agent。例如，RecMind [34] 与 MACRec [35] 引入了模块化的推理结构，实现基于规划的推荐；其他工作则探索将 LLM 嵌入推荐流水线的不同阶段——例如生成用户或物品表征 [48]、或作为高层决策控制器 [30]。同时，instruction tuning [44] 与 chain-of-thought prompting [24] 也被用于增强 LLM 的语义理解。尽管已有这些进展，显式的推理监督与细粒度用户建模仍未被充分研究。ThinkRec 通过将推理增强训练与个性化专家融合相结合，填补了这一空白，实现了基于结构化推理的、面向用户的个性化推荐。

paragraphs.text_en: Reasoning Model. Recent advances have transformed LLMs from passive token predictors into structured reasoning agents by incorporating process-level supervision. Techniques such as Chain-of-Thought prompting [36], ReAct [40], and Tree-of-Thoughts [39] enable models to generate intermediate reasoning steps, improving interpretability and multistep inference quality. To further reinforce reasoning capabilities, recent works have introduced process reward models [43] and self-improvement pipelines using techniques like Monte Carlo Tree Search [25] and reasoning distillation [38]. These trends define the emerging paradigm of Large Reasoning Models, which prioritize explicit, verifiable thinking processes over direct output. ThinkRec draws inspiration from this direction by
paragraphs.text_zh: 推理模型。最近的研究通过引入过程级监督，将 LLM 从被动的 token 预测器转变为结构化的推理 agent。Chain-of-Thought prompting [36]、ReAct [40]、Tree-of-Thoughts [39] 等技术使模型能够生成中间推理步骤，提高了可解释性与多步推理的质量。为进一步强化推理能力，近期工作引入了过程奖励模型 [43] 以及借助 Monte Carlo Tree Search [25] 与推理蒸馏 [38] 的自我改进流程。这些趋势共同定义了正在兴起的 Large Reasoning Models 范式，其更强调显式、可验证的思考过程而非直接输出。ThinkRec 正是从这一方向汲取灵感，

paragraphs.text_en: introducing reasoning-augmented training for recommendation, aligning to embed structured reasoning into decision making.
paragraphs.text_zh: 在推荐场景中引入推理增强训练，使结构化推理嵌入决策过程之中。

paragraphs.text_en: 3.2 Thinking Enhanced Recommendation
paragraphs.text_zh: 3.2 思考增强的推荐

paragraphs.text_en: To align recommendation with language modeling tasks, we highlight the importance of thinking activation for LLMs and propose a framework that consists of data construction and jointly training.
paragraphs.text_zh: 为了让推荐与语言建模任务对齐，我们强调对 LLM 进行思考激活的重要性，并提出了一个由数据构造与联合训练组成的框架。

paragraphs.text_en: 3.2.1 Reasoning data construction. To support LLMs for more effective reasoning, we need more textual information in addition to item titles. Given that the raw metadata often contains excessive or noisy content, directly using long-form text may hinder the understanding and inference of LLMs. To address this, we leverage a pre-trained summarization model [37] to extract key concepts from the item metadata, and retain up to 10 representative keywords to enhance the semantic representation of each item. To model more comprehensive preference information, not just liking information, we add low-scoring interactions to the history sequence as well.
paragraphs.text_zh: 3.2.1 推理数据构造。为了支撑 LLM 进行更有效的推理，我们需要在物品标题之外提供更多文本信息。考虑到原始元数据往往冗长或含噪，直接使用长文本会妨碍 LLM 的理解与推断。为此，我们利用一个预训练的摘要模型 [37] 从物品元数据中抽取关键概念，并保留至多 10 个具代表性的关键词以增强物品的语义表征。同时，为了刻画更全面的偏好信息（不只是喜欢的部分），我们也将低评分交互纳入历史序列。

paragraphs.text_en: 3.4 Staged Training
paragraphs.text_zh: 3.4 分阶段训练

paragraphs.text_en: In this section, we describe the training process. First, we train a global LoRA $\mathrm { L o R A } _ { g l o b a l }$ on the full dataset under pure text conditions. In parallel, we train a collaborative model $f _ { \psi } ( \cdot ; S )$ on the full dataset under ID-based conditions. Next, user features extracted from the collaborative model are used to group the data, and the grouped data are employed to fine-tune the last 8 layers of $\mathrm { L o R A } _ { g l o b a l }$ yielding a set of base LoRAs $\left\{ \mathrm { L o R A } _ { 1 : N } \right\}$ . Finally, leveraging the global dataset with injected collaborative signals, we train a projector $p r o j _ { \phi } ( \cdot )$ that projects collaborative embeddings into the LLM language space, while keeping $\mathrm { L o R A } _ { g l o b a l }$ fixed.
paragraphs.text_zh: 本节描述训练过程。首先，在纯文本条件下用全数据训练一个全局 LoRA $\mathrm { L o R A } _ { g l o b a l }$；同时在基于 ID 的条件下用全数据训练一个协同模型 $f _ { \psi } ( \cdot ; S )$。然后，从协同模型抽取的用户特征用于对数据分组，并用分组后的数据 fine-tune $\mathrm { L o R A } _ { g l o b a l }$ 的最后 8 层，得到一组 base LoRA $\left\{ \mathrm { L o R A } _ { 1 : N } \right\}$。最后，在保持 $\mathrm { L o R A } _ { g l o b a l }$ 不变的前提下，使用注入了协同信号的全局数据集训练一个 projector $p r o j _ { \phi } ( \cdot )$，将协同 embedding 映射到 LLM 的语言空间。

paragraphs.text_en: 4.1.1 Datasets. We conduct experiments on three datasets: ML1M (MovieLens-1M)2, Yelp (Yelp Open Dataset)3, and Book (the “Book” subset of the Amazon Product Review dataset)4. To better simulate real-world recommendation scenarios and avoid data leakage [15], we split each dataset into training, validation, and testing sets according to interaction timestamps. Specifically, for Amazon-Book, due to its large scale, we retain interactions from 2017 only, using the first 10 months for training and the last 2 months for validation and testing. For Yelp, we retain interactions from 2010 to 2022, assigning the first 10 years to training and the last 2 years to validation and testing. For ML1M, we keep interactions from the most recent 20 months, with the first 10 months for training and the remaining 10 months for validation and testing. To address sparsity in Book and Yelp, we filter out users and items with fewer than 20 interactions. The statistics of the processed datasets are summarized in Table 1, where $\mu$ and $\sigma$ denote the mean and standard deviation of user interactions, respectively.

paragraphs.text_en: 4.3.1 Ablation Studies (RQ2). To evaluate the importance of explicit reasoning in recommendation, we ablate the "thinking" component of ThinkRec, which disables reasoning supervision (w/o think). As shown in Table 4, this leads to significant performance degradation in all datasets. For example, UAUC on the Book dataset drops from 0.5705 to 0.4692. Interestingly, this is even lower than the variant in which both thinking and expert mechanisms are removed (w/o both). This counterintuitive result suggests that, in the absence of thinking, the recommendation task degenerates into binary classification, where multi-expert modeling risks overfitting superficial interactions and thereby undermining generalization.
paragraphs.text_zh: 4.3.1 消融实验（RQ2）。为评估显式推理在推荐中的重要性，我们移除 ThinkRec 的 "思考" 组件、关闭推理监督（w/o think）。如表 4 所示，所有数据集上的性能都显著下降，例如 Book 数据集上的 UAUC 从 0.5705 降至 0.4692，甚至低于同时移除思考与专家机制的变体（w/o both）。这一反直觉的结果说明，在缺乏思考的情况下推荐任务退化为二元分类，多专家建模反而容易过拟合表层交互模式，损害泛化。

paragraphs.text_en: We then assess the contribution of the expert personalization module, which removes the latent-feature-based user grouping and experts fusion mechanism (w/o experts). As shown in Table 4, this also leads to consistent performance drops—for instance, MAP@5 on Yelp falls from 0.2826 to 0.2791. Notably, only when thinking is enabled does multi-expert modeling begin to show substantial benefits. With reasoning supervision, group-specific LoRA modules can effectively specialize in distinct user groups, capturing finegrained preference signals that would otherwise be blurred in the global model. These findings highlight the consistency and complementarity between thinking and multi-expert modeling, providing a semantically rich space that allows user grouping to generalize rather than overfit, enabling expert models to move beyond surface interaction patterns and capture deeper preference semantics.
paragraphs.text_zh: 随后我们评估专家个性化模块的贡献，移除基于潜在特征的用户分组与专家融合机制（w/o experts）。如表 4 所示，性能同样持续下降，例如 Yelp 上 MAP@5 从 0.2826 降至 0.2791。值得注意的是，只有在启用思考时多专家建模才能展现出实质性收益：有了推理监督，分组特定的 LoRA 模块才能真正聚焦于不同用户群体，捕捉到那些在全局模型中会被模糊化的细粒度偏好信号。这表明思考与多专家建模之间高度一致且互补——推理提供的语义丰富空间使用户分组得以泛化而非过拟合，使专家模型能超越表层交互、刻画更深层的偏好语义。

paragraphs.text_en: Analysis of the grouping features. Under a fixed two-group setting, we further investigate how the choice of user grouping features affects model performance. This trend highlights the importance of semantic decoupling among expert groups. paragraphs.text_en: 4.3.4 Inference Efficiency. Although ThinkRec leverages multiple LoRA-tuned experts during training, inference requires only a single LLM forward pass with the fused LoRA adapter (via weighted sum of a few small matrices), and a lightweight gating computation over user embeddings. Because LoRA adapters add only a small fraction $( < ~ 1 . 5 \% )$ of extra parameters and incur negligible runtime overhead, the overall latency increase is minimal (empirically $< 1 0 \%$ relative to a standard LoRA-tuned LLM) while delivering substantially richer, interpretable outputs.
paragraphs.text_zh: 4.3.4 推理效率。尽管 ThinkRec 在训练时利用了多个 LoRA 微调的专家，推理阶段只需一次 LLM 前向传递（通过对若干小矩阵加权求和得到融合后的 LoRA adapter），加上一次基于用户 embedding 的轻量级门控计算。由于 LoRA adapter 仅引入很小一部分（$<1.5\%$）额外参数、运行时开销可忽略，整体延迟增加非常有限（实验中相对于标准 LoRA-tuned LLM $<10\%$），却能产出更丰富、更可解释的输出。

paragraphs.text_en: 5 Conclusion
paragraphs.text_zh: 5 结论

paragraphs.text_en: The core contribution of this research is advancing LLM-based recommendation systems from an intuitive, matching-based "System 1" paradigm to a "System 2" paradigm characterized by explicit reasoning. Through our proposed thinking activation mechanism and instance-wise expert fusion strategy, ThinkRec deeply couples the recommendation task with the reasoning capabilities of language models. Experimental results confirm that this approach not only significantly improves recommendation accuracy but, crucially, enhances system transparency and user trust by generating traceable reasons. We believe that future research will move towards deeper cognitive insights or exploring training-free mechanisms like activation steering for personalized reasoning[16], enabling systems to perform more rigorous logical reasoning. Moreover, based on the principles of automatic and personalized selection, deeper levels of Collective Intelligence, such as in Multi-Agent Systems, can be explored. ThinkRec builds a solid bridge for this leap. We provide the ethical use of data in Appendix A.
paragraphs.text_zh: 本研究的核心贡献是将基于 LLM 的推荐系统从直觉式、基于匹配的 "System 1" 范式推向以显式推理为特征的 "System 2" 范式。通过我们提出的思考激活机制与实例级专家融合策略，ThinkRec 将推荐任务与语言模型的推理能力深度耦合。实验结果证实，这一方法不仅显著提升了推荐准确率，更为重要的是通过生成可追溯的理由增强了系统透明度与用户信任。我们相信，未来研究将朝向更深层的认知洞察，或探索 activation steering [16] 等无需训练的个性化推理机制，使系统能够进行更严格的逻辑推理；此外，基于自动化、个性化选择的原则，更深层次的集体智能（如 Multi-Agent 系统）也值得探索。ThinkRec 为这一跃迁搭建了坚实的桥梁。我们关于数据使用的伦理说明见 Appendix A。
